title: Sets & Set Operations
goal: Count elements correctly (nested sets, repeats), read set-builder notation over ℕ, ℙ, ℤ, ℝ, and compute `∪ ∩ \ ⊕ ᶜ` step by step, including Quiz 1 Q4-style expressions.
magic: `{x ∈ X : P(x)}`: domain first. `0 ∈ ℕ`, `0 ∉ ℙ`.
`∪` or, `∩` and, `\` but not, `⊕` exactly one, `ᶜ` not (relative to the universe).
Multi-step: list every set, innermost bracket first.

blocks.title: 💡 Learn it, one idea at a time
A set is a bag of distinct things; order and repeats don't count
blocks.summary: Only membership matters. `{a, b} = {b, a, a}`. A set inside a set counts as ONE element.
blocks.picture: A guest list: writing "Ana, Ben, Ana" doesn't invite Ana twice, and the order you wrote the names doesn't matter. A plus-one group written as "(Cal and Dee)" counts as one entry on the list.
blocks.official: A **set** is a collection of elements (Week 1, slide 21). `{a, b, c} = {a, a, b, b, b, c} = {b, c, a}`: three elements. `{a, {a}}` has **two** elements; `{a, b, {a, b}}` has three; `{}` has zero; `{{{}}}` has one; `{{}, {{}}}` has two. `|X| = #(X) = card(X)` is the number of elements. Always `a ≠ {a}` (slide 22). The empty set is `{ }`, also written `∅`.

steps: List the **different** elements one by one.
`{1}`: a set, one element of the outer set.

tries.why: `∅` and `{∅}` are different things: one is empty, the other contains something.

check.expr: len({frozenset(), frozenset({frozenset()})})
len({frozenset({1,2}), frozenset({2,1}), 3})

tries.a: **No.** It has one element (the empty set).
tries.why: An empty box inside a box: the outer box isn't empty.

check.expr: len({frozenset()})

trap.tempting: `{a, {a}}` has one element because both are "a".
trap.correct: `a` and `{a}` are different objects (slide 22: `a ≠ {a}`), so the set has **two** elements.
trap.test: Wrap each top-level element in a box. Count boxes.

blocks.title: Set-builder notation and the number sets
blocks.summary: `{x ∈ X : P(x)}` = everything in `X` that passes the test `P`. Watch which `X`: ℕ starts at 0, ℙ at 1.
blocks.picture: A database query: `SELECT x FROM X WHERE P(x)`. Change the table `X` and the same condition returns different rows.
blocks.official: Sets can be given by a property: `S = {x : x ∈ X and P(x)} = {x ∈ X : P(x)}` (Week 1, slide 22). Number sets (slide 23): `ℕ = {0, 1, 2, …}` (**includes 0**), `ℙ = {1, 2, …}` (also `ℕ>0`, `ℤ>0`), `ℤ`, `ℚ = {m/n : m, n ∈ ℤ, n ≠ 0}`, `ℝ`. They nest: `ℙ ⊂ ℕ ⊂ ℤ ⊂ ℚ ⊂ ℝ` (slide 34). Note: by these definitions `{n ∈ ℕ : 2 | n}` also contains 0.

watch.q: List `{x ∈ ℝ : x² = 16}` and `{n ∈ ℕ : n² = 16}`.

check.expr: sorted(n for n in range(0, 50) if 2 < n < 6)
sorted(n for n in range(-50, 50) if 2 < abs(n) < 6)

tries.why: The positive divisors of 12. (0 isn't included: `0 ∤ 12`.)

check.expr: sorted(n for n in range(0, 50) if divides(n, 12))
divides(5, 0)

trap.correct: In this course `ℕ = {0, 1, 2, …}`. The positive integers are `ℙ`.
trap.test: When a set is built from ℕ, ask: does 0 pass the test?

blocks.magic: `{x ∈ X : P(x)}`: domain first, then the test. `0 ∈ ℕ`, `0 ∉ ℙ`.

blocks.title: How many elements? Watch for repeated values
blocks.summary: A formula can produce the same value from different inputs. Count the distinct **values**, not the inputs.
blocks.picture: Asking 5 people their favourite colour and getting "red, blue, red, red, blue": 5 answers, but only 2 colours.
blocks.official: Lecture exercise 1.3.2 (Week 1, slides 24–25): `|{1/n ∈ ℚ : n ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4}}| = 4` (no repeated values), `|{n² − n ∈ ℕ : n ∈ {0, …, 4}}| = 4` (one repetition), `|{2 + (−1)ⁿ : n ∈ ℕ}| = 2`.

tries.why: The values alternate `1, −1, 1, −1, …`: only two distinct values.

check.expr: len({(-1)**n for n in range(100)})
len({n % 3 for n in range(100)})
len({abs(n) for n in range(-3, 4)})

trap.tempting: The set has as many elements as there are inputs.
trap.correct: Different inputs can give the **same** value, and a set keeps only one copy.
trap.test: Write out the values, then cross out repeats.

blocks.title: Union and intersection (OR and AND for sets)
blocks.summary: `A ∪ B`: in A or B (or both). `A ∩ B`: in both. Disjoint: `A ∩ B = ∅`.
blocks.picture: Two group chats. Union: everyone who's in at least one chat. Intersection: people in both chats.
blocks.official: Union `A ∪ B` and intersection `A ∩ B` (Week 1, slide 26). If `A` is the set of `x` with property `a(x)` and `B` those with `b(x)`: `A ∪ B` = elements satisfying `a` **or** `b`; `A ∩ B` = satisfying `a` **and** `b`. `A`, `B` are **disjoint** if `A ∩ B = ∅`.

check.expr: {n for n in range(1, 100) if n % 2 == 0} & {n for n in range(1, 100) if n % 3 == 0} == {n for n in range(1, 100) if n % 6 == 0}

tries.why: Adding nothing changes nothing; sharing with nothing leaves nothing (slide 29).

check.expr: all((A | set()) == A and (A & set()) == set() for A in [set(), {1}, {1,2}])

trap.tempting: `A ∩ B` is what you get when you put A and B together.
trap.test: `∪` looks like a cup that collects everything; `∩` like a bridge over what's in both.

blocks.title: Difference, symmetric difference and complement
blocks.summary: `A \ B`: in A but not B. `A ⊕ B`: in exactly one. `Aᶜ`: everything in the universe that's not in A.
blocks.picture: Your playlist minus your friend's: `A \ B`. Songs only one of you likes: `A ⊕ B`. Every song on the platform you **don't** have: `Aᶜ`.
blocks.official: Week 1, slide 27: `A \ B` (difference; logically "`a` but not `b`"). `A ⊕ B ≝ (A \ B) ∪ (B \ A)` (symmetric difference; "xor"). `Aᶜ`: complement with respect to the **universe** ("not `a`"). Also `A \ B = A ∩ Bᶜ`.

steps: `A \ B`: in A, not in B → `{1, 2}`.

tries.why: Everything in U that's in neither.
Lecture exercise 1.4.7: nothing is in exactly one copy of A; everything in A is in exactly one of A, ∅.

check.expr: all((A ^ A) == set() and (A ^ set()) == A for A in [set(), {1}, {1, 2, 3}])

tries.q: `{1, 2, 3}ᶜ` if the universe is `ℙ`? If it's `{1, 2, 3, 4}`?
tries.why: The complement depends on the universe.

trap.tempting: `A \ B` and `B \ A` are the same.
trap.correct: `A \ B` keeps A's leftovers; `B \ A` keeps B's. `⊕` joins both.
trap.test: Say it aloud: "A minus B" = start from A.

blocks.magic: `\` = but not. `⊕` = exactly one. `ᶜ` = not, relative to the universe.

blocks.title: Multi-step set calculations (the Quiz 1 Q4 shape)
blocks.summary: List each set first (only the part that matters), then do the operations from the inside out.
blocks.picture: Following a recipe: prep every ingredient first (chop, measure), then combine. Don't combine half-prepped ingredients.
blocks.official: For expressions like `(Sᶜ ∩ R) \ T` over the universe `ℙ`: (1) list `R`, `S`, `T` explicitly (an infinite set can stay as a pattern, e.g. `{3, 6, 9, …}`), (2) compute the innermost bracket, (3) apply the outer operation. The final answer is usually small because `∩ R` cuts everything down.

watch.q: Universe `ℙ`. `R = {x ∈ ℙ : x ≤ 15}`, `S = {x ∈ ℙ : 3 | x}`, `T = {x ∈ ℙ : x | 30}`. Compute `(Sᶜ ∩ R) \ T`.

tries.q: Universe `ℙ`. `R = {x ∈ ℙ : x < 20}`, `S = {x ∈ ℙ : x is odd}`, `T = {x ∈ ℙ : x | 36}`. Compute `(S ∩ R) \ T`.

check.expr: sorted(({x for x in range(1, 200) if x % 2} & set(range(1, 20))) - {x for x in range(1, 200) if 36 % x == 0})

tries.why: `Sᶜ ∩ R` = even numbers below 20; keep those dividing 36.

check.expr: sorted((set(range(1, 20)) - {x for x in range(1, 200) if x % 2}) & {x for x in range(1, 200) if 36 % x == 0})

tries.q: Universe `ℕ`. `R = {x ∈ ℕ : x ≤ 10}`, `S = {x ∈ ℕ : x is even}`, `T = {x ∈ ℕ : x | 12}`. Compute `(R \ S) ⊕ (T ∩ R)`.
tries.why: `R \ S = {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}` (0 is even, so it's in S). `T ∩ R = {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}`. In exactly one: 5, 7, 9 and 2, 4, 6.

check.expr: sorted((set(range(0, 11)) - {x for x in range(0, 200) if x % 2 == 0}) ^ ({x for x in range(1, 200) if 12 % x == 0} & set(range(0, 11))))

trap.tempting: Compute the complement `Sᶜ` only inside `R`, then forget which universe you're in.
trap.correct: `Sᶜ` is relative to the stated universe. It only becomes small **after** you intersect with `R`.
trap.test: Write the universe at the top of your working.

blocks.magic: List every set, then innermost bracket first.

check.expr: len({'a', 'b', frozenset({'a','b'}), frozenset({'a'})})

items.why: In the first, not the second.

check.expr: sorted(n for n in range(0, 50) if n*n < 10)

items.why: Only 3 in A is a multiple of 3. `A \ C` removes the non-multiples of 3, leaving 3.

check.expr: sorted({2,3,4,5} & {n for n in range(1, 100) if n % 3 == 0})
sorted({2,3,4,5} - {n for n in range(1, 100) if n % 3})

items.why: B and C split ℙ between them. `A ⊕ C = (A \ C) ∪ (C \ A) = {3} ∪ (C without 2, 4, 5)`.

check.expr: sorted(({2,3,4,5} - {n for n in range(1, 30) if n % 3}) | ({n for n in range(1, 30) if n % 3} - {2,3,4,5}))[:8]
len({n*n - 2*n for n in range(4)})

items.q: Are `{n ∈ ℤ : n mod 4 = 1}` and `{n ∈ ℤ : n mod 4 = 3}` disjoint?
items.why: A number has only one remainder mod 4.

blocks.sub: Quiz 1 style (a variation of Problem set 1, Q4): compute a set expression over ℙ. Original sets.

items.q: Universe `ℙ`. `R = {x ∈ ℙ : x ≤ 18}`, `S = {x ∈ ℙ : x is even}`, `T = {x ∈ ℙ : x | 18}`. Compute `(S ∩ R) \ T`.

check.expr: sorted(({x for x in range(1, 200) if x % 2 == 0} & set(range(1, 19))) - {x for x in range(1, 200) if 18 % x == 0})

items.why: Remove every even number and every divisor of 18 (1, 3, 9 are the odd ones).

check.expr: sorted(set(range(1, 19)) - ({x for x in range(1, 200) if x % 2 == 0} | {x for x in range(1, 200) if 18 % x == 0}))

items.why: `S ⊕ T`: even non-divisors of 18, plus odd divisors of 18 (1, 3, 9). Then keep those `≤ 18`.

check.expr: sorted(({x for x in range(1, 200) if x % 2 == 0} ^ {x for x in range(1, 200) if 18 % x == 0}) & set(range(1, 19)))

items.q: Universe `ℙ`. `R = {x ∈ ℙ : 5 ≤ x ≤ 25}`, `S = {x ∈ ℙ : 4 | x}`, `T = {x ∈ ℙ : x | 60}`. Compute `R \ (S ∪ T)`.
items.why: From 5 … 25 remove multiples of 4 (8, 12, 16, 20, 24) and divisors of 60 (5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20).

check.expr: sorted(set(range(5, 26)) - ({x for x in range(1, 200) if x % 4 == 0} | {x for x in range(1, 200) if 60 % x == 0}))
len({frozenset({frozenset()}), frozenset({frozenset(), frozenset({frozenset()})}), frozenset(), frozenset({frozenset()})})
len({n // 2 for n in range(10)})

items.q: Universe `ℤ`. `A = {n ∈ ℤ : n² < 20}`, `B = {n ∈ ℤ : n ≥ 0}`. Compute `A \ B` and `A ∩ Bᶜ`. Why are they equal?
items.a: **Both are `{−4, −3, −2, −1}`.** `A \ B = A ∩ Bᶜ` always: "in A but not in B".

check.expr: sorted({n for n in range(-50, 50) if n*n < 20} - {n for n in range(-50, 50) if n >= 0})

items.q: Give sets `A`, `B` with `A ∪ B = A ∩ B`. What must be true?
items.why: `A ∩ B ⊆ A ⊆ A ∪ B`, so if the ends are equal, everything in between is equal too.

check.expr: all(((A | B) == (A & B)) == (A == B) for A in Pow({1,2}) for B in Pow({1,2}))
len({3, frozenset({3}), frozenset({3, 3})})
sorted(n for n in range(-9, 10) if abs(n) <= 1)

items.q: Universe `ℙ`, `R = {x ≤ 10}`, `S` = multiples of 3, `T` = divisors of 10. `(Sᶜ ∩ R) \ T`?

check.expr: sorted(((set(range(1, 200)) - {x for x in range(1, 200) if x % 3 == 0}) & set(range(1, 11))) - {1, 2, 5, 10})

lines: Sets: distinct elements, no order. `|X|` counts top-level elements.
Set-builder `{x ∈ X : P(x)}`. `ℙ ⊂ ℕ ⊂ ℤ ⊂ ℚ ⊂ ℝ`, and ℕ includes 0.
